content.title: The Rights of People
content.subtitle: The Mistake Allah Will Not Forgive!
content.body:
While walking, a gust of toxic smoke suddenly hits your face, or your foot almost touches dirty phlegm or betel saliva on the pavement. How do you feel then? Doesn't annoyance or a silent sigh escape your heart?

Dear brothers and sisters in faith, have you ever asked yourself—is another person suffering silently from my careless behavior?

Many of us regularly pray five times, weep in prostration, and keep voluntary fasts. But outside worship, in practical life, we forget that Islam is not just rituals on a prayer mat; it means total peace and safety for all creation.

Your Brief Pleasure, Another’s Agony!

Standing in crowded streets, on footpaths, or beside buses, people smoke thoughtlessly. For you, it is brief pleasure. But consider how an ailing elderly person nearby chokes on that smoke, or how a child struggles for breath. Can we answer for the silent agony our thoughtlessness causes them?

Littering and Spitting Everywhere

Throwing betel juice, mucus, or trash on corners, stairs, or from vehicle windows seems trivial to us. Yet the Prophet ﷺ said faith has over seventy branches, one being the removal of harmful things from walkways (Tirmidhi: 2614). He even deemed spitting in mosques a grave sin. When clearing paths is faith, how can we make them filthy and painful?

Snatching Peace for Personal Ease Is Oppression

Speaking loudly on phones inside buses, trains, or hospitals, or honking blaring horns in traffic, distressing sick pedestrians—these are not minor flaws. Trampling others' boundaries and stealing their peace violates human rights. Islam gives none the right to ruin another’s life for personal comfort.

Bankrupt Despite Mountains of Good Deeds

Our beloved Prophet ﷺ once asked his companions, "Do you know who is truly bankrupt?" They replied, the one without money or property. He said, "The truly bankrupt in my nation is he who brings abundant prayers, fasts, and charity on Judgment Day; yet he abused, slandered, usurped wealth, or hurt others unlawfully. His good deeds will pay off these victims. When merits finish, their sins will be loaded upon him, and he will be cast face-down into Hell." (Muslim: 2581)

Allah may forgive violations of His rights through mercy. But human rights are a trust; unless the aggrieved person forgives wholeheartedly, even Allah will not pardon it.

A true believer is one from whose hands, tongue, and slightest actions every creation remains entirely secure. Let us restrain our thoughtless habits today. May our footsteps bring relief to others, not silent curses.
